evidence:
The defining browser execution is genuinely graded: frozen task tests/gates/render/judge.toml:25 requires a newly authored marker in both preview and console, and tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:120,128-134 independently exercises authored JS/HTML. Server-backed reload is also well covered: tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-29 requires a new normal UI write, observed server record, independent clean-context retrieval and a further reload; server-rendered records are expressly valid. tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:414-417 tests two separate saved records. Actual installed-MCP evidence in row29-mcp-probe/observations.json records marker row29-mcp-1790834158048 executing, a 201 UI save, original-only localStorage absent from the clean context, and matching fields/server responses before and after reload. That artifact SHA256 is ba10bfd001272d5f0db2f2d7cfdf6fadf6e6652dd1fe2b1d6fe49aff5067b181; all 50 source-binding files match the frozen task.

The required process durability is not reliably proven. Public environment/instructions/integration.md:9 expressly requires complete process restart survival. The scored cw_process_restart_durability descriptor at tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:364 and S22 at tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:426-428 rely on restart_app reporting a completed restart. However, frozen tests/test.sh:154-159 sends TERM and waits at most 50 x 0.1 seconds without requiring old-group death; :160-178 launches a replacement then accepts any HTTP listener without checking the new PID is alive. tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:45-47 converts helper exit 0 into the claim that the server was relaunched.

This is confirmed by indexed raw control qc/proposals/coldwater-shared-harness/evidence/results.json, original/term_ignored: bash /tmp/harness-proposal-controls/original-term_ignored/app-restart.sh exited 0 after 5.707 seconds; old_pid=34, new_pid=100, old_alive=true; the post-call HTTP body still identifies pid 34 and memory=volatile-marker. Its app-restart.log shows EADDRINUSE for the replacement followed by app-restart pid=100 ready=1. The fixture installs process.on('SIGTERM',()=>{}). I verified the result SHA256 602a0a7c49b5e8d91f00d3162624563ac46de941029d47754c73aaac58cec637 and every original-term_ignored artifact against the current index. The recorded original test.sh SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa equals the frozen current test.sh. The generated failing helper is byte-identical to the current extracted restart template after only its documented path substitutions (helper SHA256 8e6ea49c9ea93a45f3bc0d9963a10e6cf3b266287adc76c525c8ce426510f21e). Proposed-patch controls do not clear current bytes.

Positive evidence is preserved: current golden pre/post browser artifacts and actual-restart.json show a genuine normal restart from PID 16 to 347, all six recorded records surviving, Primary revision 2 surviving then advancing to 3, and five example entries retaining their multiplicities. The actual-restart artifact SHA256 is 8ad9a4a2e7aada61c4f4a45a07574b540de4e9c0fb7f9ff9f2c8556bc5080ada; the post-results artifact SHA256 is c6643004926913c89df7cac102412e49236f4416598e1ac1a4e8082d37c7e945. The 22 actual golden app files and functional prompt/judge hashes match the frozen source. This normal-case success does not refute the false-restart counterexample.

Conforming alternative check: a server-rendered library using its own field names, with changed display ordering but stable saved identity/title/filename/source/revision, is explicitly accepted by Constraints and S22; I found no requirement for JSON endpoints, same-origin backing or sign-in. A dead Run or client-only library cannot satisfy the authored-execution/clean-context evidence. The remaining failure is specifically the helper allowing volatile server memory to masquerade as process-durable state. Evidence scope is browser/product observations and a reused exact-source synthetic helper control, not a measured configured judge result, Oracle score, target-model score or portal result.
counterexample: A real code playground stores its shared snippet identities, fields and revisions only in a Node in-memory map and installs a SIGTERM handler that leaves its HTTP server alive. Authored execution, ordinary Save/load, browser reload and independent-context retrieval can all work. On S22, the frozen helper waits five seconds, starts a replacement that exits with EADDRINUSE, and reports success because the old process still answers. Every saved record and revision then re-reads unchanged from the original volatile map, falsely satisfying the requested complete-process durability observation. The exact-source term_ignored control empirically demonstrates this survival and false success; a full graded playground variant was not run.
suggested_fix: Obtain a shared-template repair that bounds termination and verifies the old process group is gone, then requires the replacement PID to remain alive while readiness is established before restart_app can report success; preserve current template files pending that authorized change, freeze a new candidate, and rerun normal, TERM-resistant and failed-replacement persistence controls.
